description:
RE-VERIFIED 2026-09-02 against origin/main `a3a9761d1209165e5230625b9347cf6b0ad09b83`. The old Enum.reduce/tuple-accumulator diagnosis was false: the irreducible defect is the missing `Kernel.elem/2` language surface.

## Reproducer

```fz
fn main(), do: dbg(elem({1, 2}, 0))
```

`fz2 run`, `fz2 interp`, and `fz2 build` all exit 1 before backend execution with:

```text
error[lower/unbound]: compiler2 lowering found unresolved direct runtime callee elem/2
```

The same failure occurs when the tuple parameter is explicitly `any`. Capturing `&elem/2` fails as an unresolved captured runtime function. `Kernel.elem/2` does not resolve to an implementation either. Elixir 1.19.4 prints 1 for `elem({1, 2}, 0)` and 2 for index 1; negative/out-of-range indices and non-tuples raise.

## Cause / ownership

Runtime builtins are ordinary lazy runtime-library source, not a separate builtin registry. `src/modules/runtime_library/runtime.fz` omits `elem/2` from the exact Kernel import list, and `kernel.fz` defines neither `Kernel.elem/2` nor a backing runtime operation. Bare-call lowering therefore reaches `resolve_runtime_function` and reports `lower/unbound`.

The existing `TupleField` IR is only an implementation ingredient, not the public operation: it carries a compile-time constant index and its native load is documented as safe only after a matching-arity tuple predicate. The underlying schema lookup panics on an invalid field offset. `elem/2` needs a checked dynamic boundary; routing arbitrary values/indices straight through `TupleField`/`fz_struct_get_field_ref` would turn required language errors into host panics or unsafe reads.

## Acceptance

- Kernel exports `elem/2` and the default prelude imports it, so bare `elem/2`, `Kernel.elem/2`, and `&elem/2` resolve normally.
- `elem(tuple, index)` accepts a runtime integer index and returns the selected value on interp, JIT run, and AOT build/run, including when tuple/index arrive through `any`-typed values.
- Non-tuple, non-integer, negative, and index >= arity inputs fail through the language/runtime error path on every door; no Rust panic, SIGSEGV, or unchecked schema access.
- A behavioral fixture with an Elixir oracle pins valid indices, and expect-failure coverage pins invalid type/bounds behavior on every applicable door.
- Kernel/runtime docs and the relevant runtime-boundary tests identify the checked projection owner; existing pattern/destructure `TupleField` paths remain green.
title: P2 Kernel.elem/2 is absent; add safe dynamic tuple projection on all three doors
